say: In eighteen twelve, Napoleon led four hundred and twenty two thousand men into Russia.
Almost none of them would come home.
Here is that army, drawn as a single line.
Its width is the number of men.
They crossed the border, marching east on Moscow.
And the line thins with every mile.
By the time they reached Moscow, three in four were already gone.
Then the winter came, and they turned back.
This black line is the road home.
And below it, the temperature falls.
Thirty degrees below zero. Deadlier than any battle.
At the Berezina river, the line nearly vanishes.
Of four hundred and twenty two thousand, only about ten thousand came home.
A French engineer drew this entire story in a single chart, in eighteen sixty nine.
It is still called the finest statistical graphic ever made.
